subject: Your MCP app store map
text:
Hi Frank,

Just read your post on getting Wherbi into every AI app store. The "listed is not discovered" part is very true, and the store table is the clearest one I've seen.

I run PickAPlugin (https://pickaplugin.com), a free independent directory of ChatGPT and Codex plugins, sorted by hand. If you ever extend the B2B and developer stores section, it might be a useful addition for people shipping a plugin version of their MCP server. If Wherbi gets a plugin package, I'm happy to list it for free too.

Aaron, PickAPlugin

subject: Your Codex plugins walkthrough
text:
Hi Taylor,

I liked your Codex plugins walkthrough, especially the bit about inspecting the package before installing. More people should do that.

I run PickAPlugin (https://pickaplugin.com), a free directory of ChatGPT and Codex plugins with the last update, license and install command for each. If it helps readers in the "choose a plugin for a specific job" section, feel free to link it. We also have some original data on the plugin ecosystem that's free to cite: https://pickaplugin.com/research/state-of-codex-plugins-2026

Aaron, PickAPlugin

subject: Your AI plugin directories guide
text:
Hi there,

Your guide to listing a SaaS in every AI plugin directory is really practical, and I agree with the "get referenced before you get installed" point.

I run PickAPlugin (https://pickaplugin.com), an independent, hand-sorted directory of ChatGPT and Codex plugins. Listings are free, so if Viraloop or Faceless ships a Codex plugin I'd be glad to add it. And if you ever add a line about third-party directories to the ChatGPT chapter, we'd be a fit there.

Aaron, PickAPlugin

subject: SkillMaxx + PickAPlugin
text:
Hi,

I've been reading SkillMaxx. Actually running the installs nightly and publishing why things fail is a great idea, and the Codex numbers in issue #1 were interesting.

I run PickAPlugin (https://pickaplugin.com), a smaller hand-sorted directory of ChatGPT and Codex plugins. We cover different angles, so would a simple link swap make sense? I'd happily point our readers to your install-test results. Our research page is also free to cite if it's ever useful for the newsletter: https://pickaplugin.com/research/state-of-codex-plugins-2026

Aaron, PickAPlugin
